answer: A stake-bonded identity registry is one concrete defence: every agent must lock a refundable deposit and post a signed beacon proving it controls a distinct resource, so spawning a thousand clones means funding a thousand deposits first. Votes are weighted by bond, and a fresh account carries no attested history. When a burst of lookalikes tries to ride the same tide, governance can slash their bonds and freeze payouts, and honest peers need only whisper one flag into the ledger to trigger review. The attacker's cost scales with identity count while payoff per identity stays flat.
